title: The specified field purity family, inverse orientation and counit trace at common stages
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $r\ge0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Use the actual operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Integral categories mean modules over the completed coefficient sheaf, derived complete with constructible reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; finite categories mean $D^b_{ctf}(-,A_n)$. Write $H_\Lambda(L)=Lf^*L(r)[2r]$, $G_\Lambda(L)=Rf^!L$, $P_\Lambda=Rf_!$, and $\epsilon_\Lambda:P_\Lambda G_\Lambda\to\mathrm{id}$ for the actual exceptional counit. At finite levels use the specified smooth purity map [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] and trace [def-pur-smooth-trace].

Use $D^b_c(-,E)=D^b_c(-,R)[1/\varpi]$ and the common finite-field-stage category $D^b_c(-,\Omega)$ of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. For every finite coefficient field $F$, choose the simultaneous integral natural family $\gamma_{\mathcal O_F}$ of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. At each field stage use the purity object presented by a specified normalized integral lattice and its purity component, as in [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. Denote the transported maps by $\gamma_{\Lambda,L}:H_\Lambda L\to G_\Lambda L$, for $\Lambda=E,\Omega$, and put $\eta_{\Lambda,L}=\gamma_{\Lambda,L}^{-1}$ and $t_{\Lambda,L}=\epsilon_{\Lambda,L}\circ P_\Lambda(\gamma_{\Lambda,L})$.

These are well-defined isomorphisms $\gamma,\eta$ and morphisms $t$ on the specified presentations, using one and the same normalized integral family for purity and trace. For rationalization, finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset F$, or passage to a common finite field representing an $\Omega$-object, let $C_X,C_Y$ be the corresponding coefficient functors, and use the canonical natural comparisons $a:C_XH\xrightarrow{\sim}H'C_Y$, $b:C_XG\xrightarrow{\sim}G'C_Y$, $c:C_YP\xrightarrow{\sim}P'C_X$, where a prime denotes the target coefficient stage. For every object $L$ on these domains, the actual maps satisfy
$$b_L C_X(\gamma_L)=\gamma'_{C_YL}a_L,\qquad a_L C_X(\eta_L)=\eta'_{C_YL}b_L,$$
$$C_Y(t_L)=t'_{C_YL}\,P'(a_L)\,c_{HL}.$$
The first equation uses the tensor associators, identity comparisons and triple-extension cocycles of the specified integral natural family. All three equations respect these identity and composite coefficient comparisons, and can be checked in one common finite field containing the representatives of their arrows. In particular they do not posit a reduction functor from a field to $A_n$.

source.place: Clause (6), rationalization and common-stage coefficient passage of purity and smooth trace; auxiliary coefficient-domain statement extracted from the returned split

proof.text: First check the domain of the integral input. By [lem-pur-rational-lattice-adic-domain], every integral representative in the raw rational category belongs to the derived-complete uniform finite-Tor category; this applies to both $X$ and $Y$ in the present separated finite-type setting. Apply [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] on that domain, selecting its simultaneous natural family once for all finite fields, with its specified finite reductions. For a presented lattice $L_0$, take the image of its component and its inverse under rationalization. The field-purity theorem [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] identifies this image with the specified purity component on that presentation. Thus no independent choice of a field orientation or trace has entered.

source.place: Step 1: integral lattice and its specified adic component

proof.text:
Apply [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to the integral exact linear functors and natural transformations. On a localized arrow $u/\varpi^m$, naturality is the integral equality multiplied by $\varpi^{-m}$; equations between components remain equations because localization is a functor. The localized $H,G$ and the finite-field comparisons $a,b$ are the actual ones, including map actions, by [lem-pur-rational-scalar-comparison-identification]. That statement identifies $b$ with the counit-preserving exceptional mate and retains the integral purity square and its associators. The compact-support functor is the localized one by [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and [lem-coef-rational-operations] identifies the localized exceptional adjunction with the actual one, preserving counits. Consequently, for rationalization and for finite field extension, we have both
$$b_L C_X(\gamma_L)=\gamma'_{C_YL}a_L,\qquad C_Y(\epsilon_L)=\epsilon'_{C_YL}P'(b_L)c_{GL}.$$
For the second equality at an integral extension, it is precisely the adjoint-transpose characterization in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]; localization preserves that equality.

source.place: Localized adjunction, actual compact support, counits and finite scalar extension

proof.text:
Since the components are isomorphisms, functoriality gives $C_X(\eta_L)=C_X(\gamma_L)^{-1}$. Left-compose the first equation of Step 2 by $\eta'_{C_YL}$ and right-compose it by $C_X(\eta_L)$. Cancelling the inverse pairs gives
$$a_L C_X(\eta_L)=\eta'_{C_YL}b_L.$$
The two inverse identities for $\gamma,\eta$ are likewise images of the integral inverse identities. This proves the inverse equation for precisely the chosen component, without introducing any other orientation.

source.place: Step 1: apply the coefficient functor to the isomorphism and its inverse

proof.text:
Use the counit identity of Step 2 and naturality of $c$ at $\gamma_L:HL\to GL$, namely $c_{GL}C_Y(P\gamma_L)=P'(C_X\gamma_L)c_{HL}$. With all composition read right to left, functoriality then gives
$$\begin{aligned}
C_Y(t_L)&=C_Y(\epsilon_L)C_Y(P\gamma_L)\\
&=\epsilon'_{C_YL}P'(b_L)c_{GL}C_Y(P\gamma_L)\\
&=\epsilon'_{C_YL}P'(b_L C_X\gamma_L)c_{HL}\\
&=\epsilon'_{C_YL}P'(\gamma'_{C_YL})P'(a_L)c_{HL}\\
&=t'_{C_YL}P'(a_L)c_{HL}.
\end{aligned}$$
This calculation also shows that transporting the integral composite $\epsilon P\gamma$ gives exactly the composite defining the field trace.

source.place: Last two paragraphs: counit-preserving coefficient passage; explicit trace calculation

proof.text: The identity and successive-extension equations for $a,b$ are those in [lem-pur-rational-scalar-comparison-identification]. For $c$ use [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison], the comparison by which [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] defines $b$: on $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, which contains every integral representative by Step 1, it is the identity for $F=E$, commutes with the shift comparisons, and for $E\subset F\subset L$ satisfies the tensor-associator cocycle $c_{L/E,M}\circ\alpha^Y_{P_EM}=P_L(\alpha^X_M)\circ c_{L/F,C_{F/E,X}M}\circ C_{L/F,Y}(c_{F/E,M})$. These are equations between components, so the localization of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] carries them to the rational $c$; for rationalization itself $c$ is the identity on objects of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Thus all three comparison systems are coherent. To check the inverse equation for a composite extension, substitute the two successive inverse equations and cancel the intermediate $b^{-1}b$ (equivalently invert the pasted purity square). For the trace equation substitute the two successive equations of Step 4; naturality of the second $c$ moves the image of $P'(a)$ past it. The remaining composite is the direct $c$ by its cocycle and the direct $a$ by its cocycle, the associator $H_L(\alpha^Y)$ being absorbed by naturality of $t$. Identity comparisons give identity equations. Rationalization preserves the same substitutions and cancellations.

source.place: Steps 1 and 2: retain coefficient identity and associator equations

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] to these coherent finite-stage functors and transformations. By [lem-pur-common-stage-smooth-operation-identification], the descended $H,G$, their map actions, and the components of $\gamma,\eta$ agree with the specified smooth operations and purity presentations. The descended $P$ has object $(E,P_E M)$, the compact-support prescription of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; its map on a representative $u$ over $F$ is $c_{F/E'}^{-1}P_F(u)c_{F/E}$ by the descent formula. The counits descend as compatible transformations by Step 2 and have component represented by $\epsilon_{E,L}$, since [lem-coef-rational-operations] preserves the actual exceptional counits. The finite-stage Hom adjunctions therefore induce the common-stage adjunction: on representatives apply the finite-stage bijection; the counit compatibility makes it independent of enlargement, and the inverse bijections give the inverse on the colimit. Thus this descended counit is the actual exceptional counit of the operation datum. Its composite with $P\gamma$ is represented by the same finite-stage $t$.

source.place: Common-stage representative formula and descent of compatible transformations

proof.text: Finally, by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], every arrow in any of the finitely many diagrams has a representative over some finite coefficient field; take a common overfield of those finitely many fields. Steps 2--5 give the three equations there, with the prescribed comparisons. They consequently give the equations in the common-stage category. A change of representatives gives equal arrows after some further finite extension; the coherence of Step 5 then gives the same equations. This proves well-definedness on the specified presentations, identity and composite compatibility, and the common-stage checking assertion. The construction used only integral reduction towers, their rationalizations and finite field extensions.

source.place: Step 2: passage to a common finite coefficient field
